{{Recipe}}

== Ingredients ==
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] gray morel [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], cut into [[Cookbook:Slicing|slices]] less than 1 [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] long
* ¼ cup thinly-sliced [[Cookbook:Green Onion|green onion]] tops
* ½ Tbsp dried [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley]]
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]]
* ¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ cup dry white [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
* 2 cups [[Cookbook:Whipping Cream|whipping cream]]
* ½ tsp Dijon [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]

== Procedure ==

# In a 12-inch [[Cookbook:Non-stick|non-stick]] [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]], heat the butter over medium-high heat until foaming.
# Add the morels and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]], stirring occasionally, for 15–20 minutes until slightly crispy.
# Add the onion tops, parsley, nutmeg, pepper, and salt and cook for a few minutes
# Turn up the heat, add wine, and reduce to almost a glaze
# Turn heat to medium and add the cream and mustard. Reduce slightly over slow [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] until thickened—about 10–12 minutes.
# Serve.
== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* To make this a really grand dish, add 20–24 nice-sized boiled shrimp to the sauce before serving.
